item.title: DIM (Diindolylmethane)
item.description:
What it is: DIM is a phytonutrient derived from cruciferous vegetables (especially broccoli) that supports healthy estrogen metabolism and hormonal balance. By promoting favorable estrogen metabolites, DIM supports hormonal optimization for both men and women.

Benefits

Estrogen Metabolism & Hormonal Balance

  • Supports conversion of estrogen to favorable metabolites
  • Reduces accumulation of problematic estrogen metabolites
  • Promotes healthy estrogen-to-progesterone balance
  • Supports hormonal resilience
  • Particularly valuable for women during cycling years

Detoxification Support

  • Supports Phase II liver detoxification of estrogens
  • Works with glutathione pathway
  • Supports overall detoxification capacity
  • Complements comprehensive detox strategies

Women’s Health

  • May reduce hormonal symptoms and discomfort
  • Supports mood and emotional balance
  • May improve skin clarity
  • Supports energy and vitality
  • Complements female hormonal optimization

Men’s Health

  • May support healthy testosterone levels
  • May reduce conversion of testosterone to estrogen
  • Supports male hormonal balance
  • Complements male vitality strategies

Breast Health

  • Emerging evidence for breast tissue health
  • Supports healthy estrogen metabolism
  • May reduce breast tissue changes
  • Complements breast health strategies

Dosage

Hormonal support: 100-150 mg daily Enhanced: 150-200 mg daily Full spectrum: 200-300 mg daily Timing: With meals containing fat (enhances absorption) Duration: 4-8 weeks for initial effects; 12+ weeks for full hormonal optimization

item.title: Prenatal Vitamins
item.description:
What it is: Prenatal vitamins are specially formulated supplements containing optimal levels of folic acid, iron, calcium, and DHA to support healthy pregnancy and fetal development. Not optional—medical guidelines recommend prenatal supplementation from conception through lactation to prevent birth defects and support maternal health.

item.title: Iron
item.description:
What Is Iron?

Iron is an essential mineral critical for oxygen transport, energy production, and immune function. It’s a core component of hemoglobin (in red blood cells) and myoglobin (in muscles), allowing your body to carry and utilize oxygen.

Iron deficiency is the most common nutritional deficiency worldwide, affecting an estimated 2 billion people, particularly women of childbearing age, vegetarians, endurance athletes, and those with digestive disorders.

Unlike some supplements, iron should only be taken if deficiency is confirmed through blood testing.

item.title: Nutrients Depleted by Birth Control Pills
item.description:
How Birth Control Affects Nutrients

Hormonal birth control, particularly combined oral contraceptives (the pill), can deplete several important vitamins and minerals. This isn’t a reason to avoid birth control — it’s a reason to be aware and supplement appropriately.

Why this happens:

  • Synthetic hormones increase nutrient demand
  • Liver metabolism changes affect nutrient processing
  • Some nutrients are used up faster
